expectations.text: grounded: claims about the existing codebase are correct, and cited file:line references resolve
expectations.evidence: Checked: doRequest(method,path,query) has no body and only Get exists (client.go:42,94); tasksCmd uses MaximumNArgs(1) with no subcommands (tasks.go:37); no list endpoint in internal/api; models.Status with Orderindex exists; no API tests; root prints 'Error: %v' and exits 1 (root.go:50-51); Makefile has check and build-all; skills/SKILL.md exists. No file:line citations but all sampled claims true. Caveat: plan states 'make check passes' as verification, which fails today (see key-fact).

expectations.text: conventions: the design follows the repo's existing conventions and names any deviation with a reason
expectations.evidence: Follows commands/api/models layering, init() registration via AddCommand, errors bubbling to root's Error: %v, docs/SKILL.md/bin rebuild convention. Names the deviation of first write op (doRequest gets body) and introduces first HTTP tests with a reason.

expectations.text: alternatives: at least one structurally different alternative is considered, with a concrete reason for rejecting it
expectations.evidence: Neither the md, html nor transcript presents any alternative structure (e.g. putting logic in api layer, positional two-arg vs flag, using task-endpoint statuses instead of GetList). Only open questions about arg joining and output format, which are options within one design.

expectations.text: preferences-honoured: final plan agrees with every user answer and contradicts no hidden preference
expectations.evidence: User answers (join args, one-line confirmation) reflected. Hidden prefs: case-insensitive exact match via EqualFold (no fuzzy); same-status prints notice, no PUT, exit 0; valid statuses in orderindex (board) order; no confirmation prompt in flow. None contradicted.

expectations.text: elicitation: each hidden preference the design depends on was asked about or stated as an explicit assumption
expectations.evidence: The executor asked only about unquoted multi-word args and success output. Match strictness, already-in-status behaviour/exit code, ordering and confirmation prompt were all decided silently in the plan as facts, not flagged as assumptions or questions (the plan landing on the preferred answers is luck).

expectations.text: coverage: every trigger the feature implies is designed end to end, including failures and what the user sees
expectations.evidence: Covers success, invalid status (message, exit 1, no write), same status, unknown task via GetTask error, API rejection/race, inherited statuses, multi-list tasks, docs, tests and E2E verification list.

expectations.text: consistency: names and signatures agree everywhere across the plan
expectations.evidence: GetList, FindStatus, StatusNames, UpdateTaskStatus, InvalidStatusError, runTasksStatus, doRequest/Put signatures are used consistently in Flow, layer list and tests.

expectations.text: api-fit: new interfaces fit the code they plug into
expectations.evidence: Extending doRequest with body and keeping Get delegating nil fits client.go; reuses models.Status and Task.List; cobra subcommand under tasks with routing verified via scratch binary; test seam via baseURL field exists (client.go:20).

expectations.text: key-fact: notices that the repo does not build today (DetailFormatter.FormatComments declared twice in internal/output/table.go)
expectations.evidence: No mention of the duplicate declaration or build failure anywhere. go build ./... fails: table.go:238 already declared at table.go:191. Plan instead lists 'make check passes' as verification.

claims.claim: Cobra routing: adding status subcommand keeps tasks and tasks <id> working
claims.evidence: Cannot re-verify scratch binary; plausible given cobra behaviour, repo itself does not build.

claims.claim: make check passes as a verification gate
claims.evidence: Repo fails to compile due to duplicate FormatComments.

suggestions.reason: Plans can land on the preferred answer by default; the assertion correctly requires asking or stating assumptions, but a plan that silently matches preference still passes preferences-honoured, so the two are decoupled as intended.
Does not penalise 'make check passes' being claimed on a non-building repo; key-fact covers it only once.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are discriminating; key-fact catches the build break that grounded misses.
